author: BmB
body:
The problem with most of our Avicus maps is because they are all focused on the looks. The reason G_skippy's and most of MCzone's maps are still popular is because they are made for Gameplay. Don't get me wrong, looks are important however gameplay is what attracts and interests players. These new breeds of maps look fantastic however they don't run that way. For example maps such as Quintus and Rendezvous are usually shaped, void maps however the new breed of maps are large areas of fancy building that quite often lag and make gameplay boring. 

As well as this there are far too many maps for Nebula, yes it is good to see new maps however there is an overload of them currently. I think map releases should be done like the staff applications. Closed for a month or two then opened with only a certain number of maps being allowed to make it onto the rota. This way we will stop our current overload of maps. As well as this it would mean that map creators will spend more time on their maps instead of churning them out. 

Map dev's need to be more harsh as well. You lot are too nice, maps are accepted too regularly and you don't take other maps of the rota's so gradually we get too many maps. 

I think that map creators, devs and the entire of Avicus need to change their mindset a bit. The older style of maps are less aesthetically pleasing, yet they play better. The current maps look great but unfortunately don't play that way, we need to focus on the gameplay more. This post is gathered from my and other opinions, it is not meant to offend anyone.

replies.author: StaticFaultz
replies.body:
Yes. Almost every single map on Nebula is always skybridge. If you don't have a skybridge, you lose.

The problem also carries into other gamemode divisions like Nexus. This one map with a whole circular path of ice looks sexy, but it just doesn't make any sense. There's only team to team to team combat rather than involving 4 teams (and most of the times, one team is always attacking one team).  The icy path provides no interesting and fun gameplay because it's A) slippery and the path is B) thin.

Aesthetics should not be overpowering the gameplay of a map. Neither should gameplay overpower aesthetics. It should be balanced.
